record.title: Alignment Inertia measures when system prompts and LoRA fail to override prior behavior
record.summary: The Alignment Inertia preprint measures whether system prompts and LoRA fine-tuning override each model’s observed policy behavior on cases where that behavior conflicts with a target policy. It evaluates Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 on medical-misinformation and hate-speech datasets. Zero-shot prompting leaves some conflicting cases unresolved, with results varying by model, domain and policy direction; LoRA sometimes improves and sometimes worsens override success. These are author-reported behavioral results conditional on the study’s constructed divergence zones and adaptation data, not a universal measure of prompt or fine-tuning reliability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The study evaluates two open-weight instruction-tuned models across medical misinformation and hate-speech tasks, using N=500 evaluation examples per domain and condition; override success is measured only on cases where the model’s instruction-free baseline conflicts with the target policy.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Zero-shot system prompting leaves 20.0%–49.1% of conflicting cases unresolved under the more permissive target policy across the reported model/domain conditions. Results differ by model and policy direction; LoRA improves some conditions and worsens others.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper describes behavioral results, not a mechanism proving why prior behavior persists; the results cover two open-weight models and two domains, and some medical LoRA training pools exhausted before the planned 1,500 examples.

evidence_gaps.description: Override-success and LoRA findings have not been independently reproduced with repeated seeds and additional models.
The divergence zones and policy mappings are constructed from observed baselines and selected label mappings; LoRA training pools were exhausted in some medical conditions.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, policy override resistance that differs by model, policy direction and domain could change how operators assess controllability before deploying models under a policy different from their training prior. The study covers only two open-weight models and two domains and does not establish a universal failure rate.
limitations: Author-reported results; no independent reproduction was conducted.
Only two open-weight models and two policy domains were evaluated; results do not establish behavior for closed models or deployment settings.
Override success is conditional on empirically constructed policy-divergence cases and the chosen policy prompts and label mappings.
Some medical LoRA conditions exhausted the training pool well below the planned 1,500 examples, which may bias results.
The paper’s behavioral audit does not establish a mechanism or universal resistance to system prompts or fine-tuning.
brief.summary: The Alignment Inertia preprint measures whether system prompts and LoRA fine-tuning override each model’s observed policy behavior on cases where that behavior conflicts with a target policy. It evaluates Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 on medical-misinformation and hate-speech datasets. Zero-shot prompting leaves some conflicting cases unresolved, with results varying by model, domain and policy direction; LoRA sometimes improves and sometimes worsens override success. These are author-reported behavioral results conditional on the study’s constructed divergence zones and adaptation data, not a universal measure of prompt or fine-tuning reliability.

technical.claimed_result: Across Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 on medical-misinformation and hate-speech datasets, zero-shot system prompts do not override every observed policy conflict. Under the permissive target policy, the reported residual inertia is 20.0%–49.1%; LoRA effects vary by model, domain and policy direction, including regressions.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint documents the protocol, datasets, models and author-reported measurements. No independent reproduction was performed.
technical.mechanism: The study defines each model’s empirical policy from an instruction-free baseline and measures override success only on examples where the target policy conflicts with that baseline. It compares zero-shot system prompting with LoRA adaptation and uses TRAK to analyze adaptation-example influence.
technical.novelty: An intervention-relative audit of whether downstream policy instructions override an empirically observed model behavior, separating prompt-time control from LoRA changes and measuring both permissive and restrictive policy shifts.
technical.regime: Two open-weight models (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2); medical misinformation and hate speech; 500 evaluation examples per domain/condition; selected policy mappings and divergence zones. LoRA used target-policy examples but exhausted some medical pools below the 1,500-example target.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes prompts, datasets, sample sizes and adaptation settings. the research desk did not reproduce the study; repeated-seed and independent-model validation remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Instruction-free empirical baseline and the same model under zero-shot system prompting, compared with LoRA adaptation on target-policy examples. Measures are conditional on observed policy conflicts rather than a model-wide safety score.

brief.title: Alignment Inertia measures when system prompts and LoRA fail to override prior behavior
brief.why_it_matters: An operator may need to make a model more permissive or restrictive than its observed training prior. If the reported, direction-dependent resistance replicates, testing controllability on actual policy conflicts could expose cases that a generic instruction-following score misses. The study’s small model/domain set does not establish behavior across providers or deployments.
